title_tag: 10 Best Hotels in JBR, Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: JBR hotels from €116 to €620 a night: beachfront resorts, Walk towers and apartments compared on price, beach access, breakfast and room size.
h1_main: 10 Best Hotels in JBR (Jumeirah Beach Residence) in 2026
author_role: 10 JBR hotels compared on nightly price, beach access, breakfast, room size and location score
lead: For most people the right JBR hotel is the Sofitel Dubai Jumeirah Beach at €174 a night: it sits on The Walk with the beach in front, scores 9.2, and extra beds and cots for kids are free. On a tighter budget, Mövenpick Hotel Jumeirah Beach gets you a 5-star room for €136 a short walk back from the sand, and Ramada JBR is the cheapest solid stay at €116. If price is no object, The Ritz-Carlton's private beach and six pools start at €620.

All 10 were compared for the same night on price, guest score, location score, beach and pool, what breakfast costs and the size of the cheapest room. Use the filters for beachfront, suites and apartments, families, couples or €150 and under, or scroll the ranking below.

review: The Sofitel is the JBR hotel for most people because it gets the location exactly right for the money. It sits on The Walk with the beach in front, steps from The Beach mall, and the JBR 2 tram stop is 500 metres away. For €174 a night you get a 5-star room with a balcony and a partial sea view, in a hotel that scores 9.2 overall and 9.6 for location.

The cheapest room is a 377 ft² Superior Twin or King with Sofitel's MyBed and a Bose sound system. That is a normal city-hotel size, not the big rooms of FIVE LUXE (657 ft²) or Amwaj Rotana (452 ft²). What you get instead is a strong food and pool setup: ten venues on site, from the A.O.C. French brasserie to the Infini Pool Lounge over the sea, and a heated outdoor pool.

For families it is quietly one of the best deals here: cots and extra beds are free, where Hilton Dubai Jumeirah, Amwaj Rotana and Le Royal Meridien charge AED 200–360 a night for an extra bed. Compared with Mövenpick (#2), you pay €38 more and move from a walk-to-the-beach tower to a beachfront one.
Catches: breakfast is not in the headline rate, and the rate excludes taxes and the Dubai tourism fee, which are added at booking.

review: Mövenpick is the value pick of JBR. €136 buys a 5-star room in a hotel that scores 9.1, and its value-for-money score (9.1) is behind only FIVE LUXE (9.2) among the 10 hotels here, level with Le Royal Meridien. The cheapest room is a 376 ft² Superior King with a balcony, the same size as the Sofitel's.

The trade-off is position. Mövenpick is described as within walking distance of the beaches rather than on them, and Dubai Marina is a 500 metre walk. You get an outdoor pool with a pool bar and a spa, but no private beach. If the beach is the reason you are choosing JBR, the Sofitel (#1) at €174 or Amwaj Rotana (#7) at €150 put you closer.

Breakfast is simple to price: €20 on the flexible rate, or a breakfast-included non-refundable rate from €150. Five venues cover the evenings, including New York Soul and The Talk buffet with theme nights.
Families should note there are no extra beds, only free cots for under-4s.

review: FIVE LUXE is the best-reviewed hotel in JBR: 9.4 overall, with 9.6 for location and comfort and 9.5 for cleanliness and facilities. It is on the Beach Walk at JBR, has its own beachfront and an infinity pool with a pool bar, and runs six restaurants and bars from Ronin (Japanese) to Playa Pacha.

The surprise is the room. The cheapest Superior Room is 657 ft², which is 75% bigger than the Sofitel's 377 ft² and bigger than Amwaj Rotana's sea-view room. You pay for it: €266 a night, €92 more than the Sofitel.

It is built for couples: the top facilities are spa, hot tub, massage and yoga, plus six places to eat and drink. If you want a quiet family resort, the Ritz-Carlton (#4) or Hilton Dubai Jumeirah (#5) fit better.
Catches: check-in only runs from 15:00 to 18:00, a AED 1,000 damage deposit is taken on a credit card on arrival, and the cot policy is unclear (ask the hotel).

review: The Ritz-Carlton is the only true resort in this list that sits right on the JBR beach. It has an extensive private beach looking at Ain Dubai, six pools and the Ritz Kids club, and the JBR towers and The Walk are a 5-minute stroll away. Rooms face the gardens and pools, with fountains in the grounds.

At €620 a night it costs more than twice the next most expensive hotel. What that buys: a 538 ft² Deluxe Room with a balcony over the gardens and pools, a rain shower and separate tub, and a spa with hot and cold plunge pools. Breakfast-included rates are available, and its flexible rates come with free cancellation and no prepayment.

For families with the budget it has the most: Ritz Kids runs supervised activities every day, there is a kids' pool, cots are free for under-3s and extra beds are free for 12+. If you want resort space for less, Le Royal Meridien (#6) has three pools and a big spa at €273.
Catches: the cheapest rooms face the garden, not the sea, and the Club Lounge is currently closed, with club benefits served in other venues.

review: Hilton Dubai Jumeirah is the JBR beach hotel built around families. It has a kids' club, a beachside playground with slides and swings, and separate family and adults-only pools a few steps from its private beach. Water sports start straight from the sand.

The €217 rate is also the only one in the top five that includes breakfast, with free cancellation and pay at the property. The Sofitel (#1) is €43 cheaper but its €174 rate has no breakfast, so the real gap is smaller. The cheapest room is a 409 ft² Deluxe King with a marble bathroom.
Twelve restaurants and bars give you choice without leaving the hotel: Villa Verano for Italian, McGettigan's for live sport, Trader Vic's, and MarBar on the roof.
Two catches: the lead guest must be 21, and extra beds cost AED 200 a night for children too. Families of four may do better with a suite at DoubleTree (#8).

review: Le Royal Meridien is the classic beach resort at the JBR end of Dubai's coast: three pools including an infinity pool, a beachfront with water sports, and a Roman-themed spa with saunas and five hammam pools. It scores 9.3, the second highest here, with 9.7 for cleanliness.
It is not on The Walk but on Al Mamsha Street, described as only a short walk to JBR. The 14 restaurants and bars, including Maya by Richard Sandoval, mean you rarely need to leave.

At €273 room only it costs about the same as FIVE LUXE. The difference is the style: FIVE LUXE is a tower hotel on the Beach Walk, Le Royal Meridien is a resort with gardens, three pools and a bigger spa. Breakfast-included rates start at €312, and the flexible rates offer free cancellation with nothing to pay until you arrive.
The cheapest Deluxe Room has a land view but sleeps three (two singles plus an extra-large double), handy for a family with one older child without paying AED 360 for an extra bed.

review: Amwaj Rotana claims the largest rooms along JBR, and the numbers back it up for the money: €150 buys a 42 m² (452 ft²) Sea View Room with a balcony facing the Gulf and Palm Jumeirah. That is 75 ft² more than the Sofitel's entry room for €24 less.

It sits on The Walk with direct access to Jumeirah Beach, about 100 steps away, and The Beach complex with water sports right at the door. The JBR 2 tram is a 3-minute walk and a free shuttle runs to the big malls, so it is easy to explore without a car.

Families get a temperature-controlled kids' pool with a water slide, and the Splashpad water park is a 5-minute walk. The four dining concepts lean fun rather than fine: Benihana, Rosso, theme nights and happy hours.
The score is the catch: 8.7 overall, a notch below the top five. If you can live without the beach on your doorstep, Mövenpick (#2) is €14 cheaper and scores 9.1.

review: DoubleTree is the only all-suite hotel on The Walk in this list, and that is the reason to book it. €232 gets you an 835 ft² One-Bedroom Suite with a separate living room, a sofa bed and a balcony. Parents get a door to close; kids get the sofa bed.

It sits on The Walk by The Beach mall, with private access to the beach, beach cabanas and its own pool, plus an infinity pool and a spa with sauna, steam room and hot tub. The JBR 2 tram is a 5-minute walk.

Breakfast-included rates for two in the same suite start at €257, and both flexible rates come with free cancellation and pay at the property. Check-in runs until midnight, useful after a late flight, and pets are allowed on request.
For two adults it is less compelling: the Sofitel (#1) is €58 cheaper, 5-star and on the same stretch. Compared with Hilton Dubai Jumeirah (#5), you trade the kids' club for a lot more space.

review: Ramada is the budget answer for JBR. €116 a night gets you a 484 ft² room, which is more floor space than the 5-star Sofitel or Mövenpick, in a hotel that scores 8.8 and 9.4 for location. It sits on the main JBR strip between The Walk and Dubai Marina.

The upgrade worth knowing about is the One-Bedroom King Suite: 1,076 ft² with a kitchenette and sofa bed from €143. For a family or a longer stay that is the cheapest suite on this page, €89 less than the DoubleTree suite.

The facilities are those of a good 4-star: a heated outdoor pool with a pool bar, a spa with hot tub and sauna, three dining outlets including Flavours of India, and 24-hour room service. Breakfast is €25 extra.

review: Suha JBR is the apartment option, and on this date it is one of the best deals on the page: €143 for a 678 ft² one-bedroom apartment with its own kitchen, breakfast included, at the members' price you get after a free sign-in. That member rate is the cheapest breakfast-included stay here; at the regular rate Mövenpick's €150 breakfast rate is cheaper.

It is in the Sadaf 3 building, overlooking The Walk, under 5 minutes on foot from Dubai Marina and about 10 minutes from the beach. The rooftop pool with sun loungers is the main shared facility; there is no spa, beach club or kids' club.

What you get instead is space and independence: a living room, a kitchen for snacks and simple dinners, daily housekeeping, and a 24-hour front desk. Free cots for babies and check-in until midnight make it easy for families.

The building is going through a phased renovation, though all facilities remain open. If you want the same space with a hotel around it, the Ramada one-bedroom suite (#9) is €143 at the regular rate, without breakfast.

guide.h2: JBR Hotels Compared: Price, Beach and Breakfast
guide.html:
All prices are the lowest nightly rate for 2 adults on the same January night, before taxes and the tourism fee. Three of them (Sofitel, FIVE LUXE and DoubleTree) were limited-time deal rates that night, and Suha's €143 is a members' price after a free sign-in. The two columns that change the real cost are breakfast and beach: Hilton Dubai Jumeirah and Suha include breakfast, and seven of the ten sit on the sand.

guide.h2: Which JBR Hotel Should You Book?
guide.html:
• First trip, want the classic JBR stay: Sofitel at €174. Beachfront on The Walk, 9.2, free kids' beds.
  • Cheapest 5-star: Mövenpick at €136, if a short walk to the beach is fine.
  • Couples who want the top score: FIVE LUXE at €266 for the 9.4 score, 657 ft² rooms and six bars and restaurants. Arrive before 18:00.
  • Couples who want a spa resort: Le Royal Meridien at €273, with the Roman spa and three pools.
  • Families with young kids: Hilton Dubai Jumeirah at €217 with breakfast and a kids' club, or The Ritz-Carlton at €620 if budget allows.
  • Families who need space: DoubleTree one-bedroom suite at €232, or the Ramada suite from €143.
  • Most room on the beach for the money: Amwaj Rotana, 452 ft² with a sea-view balcony for €150.
  • Tight budget: Ramada at €116, or Suha at €143 (member price) with breakfast and a kitchen.

If you would rather wake up over the yachts than the beach, our Dubai Marina hotels comparison covers the towers on the other side of the JBR tram line. For a resort island stay, see the best Palm Jumeirah hotels, and for every beachfront option across the city, the best beach resorts in Dubai.

guide.h2: Where to Stay in JBR, Getting Around and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Which part of JBR

The Walk, JBR's 1.7 km promenade, runs along the beach at the foot of the towers. Hotels split three ways: beachfront on The Walk (Sofitel, Hilton Dubai Jumeirah, Amwaj Rotana, DoubleTree, FIVE LUXE), resorts at the ends (The Ritz-Carlton's gardens and six pools, and Le Royal Meridien on Al Mamsha Street, a short walk from JBR), and hotels a walk from the sand (Mövenpick, Ramada and Suha), which cost less.

Getting around

The Dubai Tram runs along JBR: the JBR 2 stop is a 3-minute walk from Amwaj Rotana, 5 minutes from DoubleTree and 500 m from the Sofitel. Hilton Dubai Jumeirah is a short walk from the metro station by Dubai Marina Mall, and Jumeirah Lakes Towers metro is close to Amwaj Rotana. Mall of the Emirates is 10–15 minutes by car from most of these hotels, and Dubai International Airport about 30 minutes. Every hotel here has free parking.

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: rates exclude 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the Dubai tourism fee of AED 15–20 per room per night (AED 15 at Ramada and the DoubleTree one-bedroom suite, AED 20 at Mövenpick, Hilton, Le Royal Meridien and the Ritz-Carlton). A 10% service charge is added on top as well.
  • Breakfast: €20 at Mövenpick, €25 at Ramada; included at Hilton Dubai Jumeirah and Suha on the rates shown.
  • Extra beds: free at the Sofitel and (for 12+) the Ritz-Carlton; AED 150 at DoubleTree, AED 200 at Hilton and FIVE LUXE, AED 216 at Amwaj Rotana, AED 360 at Le Royal Meridien. Ramada charges AED 150; Mövenpick has no extra beds.
  • Deposits and age rules: FIVE LUXE takes a AED 1,000 damage deposit by card; Hilton Dubai Jumeirah requires the lead guest to be 21.

Things to do from JBR

Hilton Dubai Jumeirah and Le Royal Meridien offer water sports from their beaches, and Amwaj Rotana has the water sports at The Beach on its doorstep. If you want more speed, compare Dubai jet ski tours; for an evening on the water, see the best dinner cruises in Dubai; and for a day inland, our desert safari comparison.

faqs.q: Which JBR hotels are directly on the beach?
faqs.a: Sofitel Dubai Jumeirah Beach, Hilton Dubai Jumeirah, FIVE LUXE, Amwaj Rotana (about 100 steps to the sand), DoubleTree (private beach access) and The Ritz-Carlton (private beach) are on the beach. Le Royal Meridien is beachfront a short walk from JBR. Mövenpick, Ramada and Suha are a short walk back from it.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest good hotel in JBR?
faqs.a: Ramada by Wyndham Dubai JBR at €116 a night for a 484 ft² room, scored 8.8. The cheapest 5-star is Mövenpick Hotel Jumeirah Beach at €136, and the cheapest stay with breakfast included is Suha JBR at €143 for a one-bedroom apartment (a members' price after a free sign-in; without it, Mövenpick's €150 breakfast rate is cheaper).

faqs.q: Is it better to stay in JBR or Dubai Marina?
faqs.a: Stay in JBR if the beach is the point of the trip: several hotels open straight onto it. Dubai Marina puts you on the yacht-lined canal with the beach a walk away. The two areas sit side by side, so you can easily use both; compare options in our Dubai Marina hotels guide.

faqs.q: Which JBR hotel is best for families?
faqs.a: Hilton Dubai Jumeirah (€217 with breakfast) has a kids' club, a beachside playground and a family pool, but the lead guest must be 21. The Ritz-Carlton has Ritz Kids and six pools at €620. For space, the DoubleTree one-bedroom suite (835 ft², €232) has a sofa bed, and the Sofitel gives free extra beds. More options are in our best family resorts in Dubai.

faqs.q: Do JBR hotel prices include breakfast?
faqs.a: Usually not. Of these 10, only Hilton Dubai Jumeirah (€217) and Suha JBR (€143, member price) include breakfast in the lowest rate. Mövenpick charges €20 and Ramada €25; the Ritz-Carlton, Le Royal Meridien and DoubleTree sell breakfast-included rates at a higher price.

faqs.q: What taxes and fees are added to a JBR hotel bill?
faqs.a: Expect a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the Dubai tourism fee of AED 15–20 per night on top of the room rate. FIVE LUXE also takes a refundable AED 1,000 damage deposit on arrival.

faqs.q: Is JBR a good base for activities?
faqs.a: Yes for the water: several of these hotels run water sports straight from their beach, and Dubai Marina is next door. For more, see our scuba diving and adrenaline experiences comparisons. The tram and metro connect you to the rest of the city.

methodology: We compared 10 hotels on and beside JBR beach side by side on the lowest nightly price for 2 adults on the same January night, guest score and location score, beach access, pools, what breakfast costs, the size of the cheapest room, kids' policies and extra charges. Prices are live rates in euros before taxes and the Dubai tourism fee. Price per square foot divides the nightly rate by the size of the room it applies to. We chose a mix of beachfront resorts, tower hotels on The Walk and apartments across price levels, and left out properties with few reviews.
